How this works

1  Physics makes the truth

A storage-cell inundation model routes each storm over Meridian: curve-number runoff, capacity-limited sewers, sub-grid river channels that overtop, and a culverted watercourse that surcharges. Mass is conserved to 1e-15. Nobody labels where it floods.

2  The AI imitates it, fast

Gradient-boosted trees over features per cell — terrain, drainage, land use and rainfall routed down the catchment — trained on simulated storms and tested on ones it never saw.

3  Why not run the physics?

Every position of that rainfall slider took the simulator tens of seconds. The surrogate answers in milliseconds, so it can re-run on each radar refresh and as an ensemble. The simulator is the better model; it cannot keep up with real time.

4  Scored honestly

Held out by storm, never by map cell. Scored with CSI / POD / FAR, not accuracy — under 2% of cells flood, so "never floods" would score 98% accurate and warn nobody.

5  The Route Safety Index

A per-cell score from 0 to 100, and deliberately not the same thing as speed. It punishes shallow water far harder than a travel-time model does, ignores design speed entirely — a highway under 20 cm of water is fast and dangerous — and triples the penalty on potholes once they are submerged and a driver cannot see them. "Safest" minimises exposure to it; "fastest" minimises minutes.

6  Every route, twice

The depth regressor is fitted on log1p(depth) and back-transformed, which biases it low — so a route planned on the forecast alone can read as a comfortable drive down a road that is actually impassable. Every route here is solved on the forecast and on the physics truth, and the page says so when they disagree rather than showing you the friendlier number.

About the registry

The — households on this map are an opt-in check-in scheme, not a census: Meridian holds 4.2 M people. Residents, ages and check-in times are generated, and the names are drawn from pools — they are not real people. What is not invented is where they sit: households are placed by the population raster, so the registry is dense where the city is dense, with a floor per district so no ward vanishes.

Meridian models — km of named road — arterials and above, not every street. A household's "road access" is the distance to that modelled network, so it reads long; a real deployment would route the last few hundred metres over a full street graph. Routing itself runs in this page, using the same cost model as meridian/routing.py, verified against it by scripts/98_verify_web_routing.py.

Meridian City is synthetic — a 4.2 M-person coastal metropolis generated from procedural terrain and stream-power erosion, calibrated against a real North African Atlantic-coast metro. Coordinates are the grid's own, anchored to a nominal Atlantic origin. The method transfers to a real city; the weights do not.
